Axios Pro Rata
By Dan Primack · Aug 11, 2026
 
 
Top of the Morning
 

Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios
 

Nvidia yesterday announced plans to raise around $500 billion to help finance AI infrastructure buildouts, in partnership with six of North America's largest investment firms.

  • Much of that money is likely to come via GPU securitizations — spreading out the exposure across insurance companies, pension systems, sovereign wealth funds, and more.
  • If this gives you a pang of PTSD, you're not alone.

The big picture: Wall Street is betting America's economy on unwavering compute demand.

  • Not just this deal, but also a spate of similar financing arrangements that presume no AI lab will build a vastly more efficient mousetrap.
  • Or that data center growth won't be significantly restricted by political pressures. Or quantum computing advancements. Or something else we can't yet see, such as an unexpected increase in rare metals production that could flip chip scarcity into surplus.
  • It's not blind faith. There are some solid economics here, including how older NVIDIA chips have demonstrated collateral value. But it's also not a sure thing — exuberance can be both rational and risky.

Zoom in: The participating firms are Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR.

  • Each firm will evaluate opportunities on a case-by-case basis, and submit allocation requests to Nvidia (which "may provide a residual-value support mechanism for up to 25%").
  • Expect many of them to create internal allocation mechanisms, spreading out the opportunities within their own business units. Some firms will invest off balance sheet, some will leverage their insurance arms, some will invest out of credit funds, etc.
  • Waldemar Szlezak, KKR's head of digital infrastructure, tells me his firm has been speaking to Nvidia for over a year, but that "this iteration really picked up steam over the last month or so."

Back in time: There are lots of positive historical comparisons here, in terms of massive industrial buildouts backed by credit. Railroad systems. Airplane fleets. Automotive (in fact, this whole thing feels a bit like new-school GMAC).

  • That said, securitization trends can begin with good intentions and then cause calamity.
  • Particularly when there is structural circularity, which has become a hallmark of the AI boom.

Worthy of your time: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang this morning published a LinkedIn post, making his case for the investability of AI compute.

The bottom line: The revolution will be securitized.
 
 
The BFD
 

Illustration: Tiffany Herring/Axios
 

Francisco Partners has agreed to buy Moneris, a Canadian fintech joint venture between Royal Bank of Canada and Bank of Montreal, for C$2 billion.

Why it's the BFD: This reflects how some banks prefer to maintain merchant relationships without the costly merchant acquisition stacks.

The bottom line: "Moneris has been a cornerstone of Canadian financial infrastructure for more than 25 years, processing one in three transactions across the country at more than 325,000 points of commerce." — Steve Randall, Wealth Professional
 
 
Venture Capital Deals
 

OpenAI completed a $7b secondary share sale for current and former employees at an $852b valuation.

🚑 Vaderis Therapeutics, a Swiss biotech focused on rare vascular diseases, raised $152m in Series B funding. Goldman Sachs Alternatives and TCGX led, joined by Omega Funds, EQT Life Sciences, Perceptive Advisors, Kalehua Capital, Medicxi, and Droia. axios.link/4q7Jfn8

🚑 Epicrispr, an SF-based developer of programmable epigenetic medicines, raised $90m in Series C funding. Octagon Capital and Janus Henderson Investors led, joined by Fidelity, Cormorant Asset Management, Duquesne Family Office, Sanofi Ventures, Abrdn, Angelini Ventures, and Readout Capital. axios.link/4g6tnN6

🚑 Infinimmune, an Alameda, Calif.-based developer of antibody therapeutics, raised $75m in Series A funding. Regeneron Ventures and Playground Global led, joined by RA Capital Management, Goldcrest Capital, Forge Life Science Partners, Godfrey Capital, and Wild Tree Ventures. Existing investors Merck Global Health Innovation Fund, Everbright Biofund, Civilization Ventures, and Pear VC. axios.link/4wNDgX7

• Corma, a frontier AI lab for defensive cybersecurity, raised $60m in seed funding. Sequoia Capital led, joined by Khosla Ventures and Coatue. axios.link/4g49LcI

• Point2 Technology, a San Jose, Calif.-based maker of data center interconnect solutions, raised $60m in Series B extension funding. LB Investment led, joined by Arm and Maverick Silicon. axios.link/4bFGcg5

• Gravity, an agent-to-agent ads product, raised $30.5m in Series A funding. Lightspeed and Committed Capital led, joined by Basis Set, Caffeinated Capital, GGF, Haystack, and Logos Fund. axios.link/4cgKbjp

🚑 Bios Life, a virtual cancer surveillance startup, raised $25m in seed funding from Redmile, Vsquared Ventures, and Kindred Capital. axios.link/3TOzQVF

• Axle, a clearinghouse for insurance data, raised $17.5m in Series A funding, per Axios Pro. Base10 Partners led, joined by Gradient, YC, and Stage 2 Capital. axios.link/3UpDIfS

🚑 Remedium Bio, a Boston-based protein therapeutics biotech, is raising $10m in Series A funding. Lifespan Vision Ventures will lead, joined by Eli Lilly and HKX Capital. axios.link/4cA7GnE

• Discovered Materials, an Indian developer of AI agents for finding new chip materials, raised $9m in seed funding from backers like Lightspeed India Partners and Peak XV Partners. axios.link/4q5txsC

• Alloy Robotics, an SF-based AI data platform for robotics teams, raised $8m in seed funding at an $80m valuation. Square Peg led, joined by Blackbird, Airtree, and Skip Capital. usealloy.ai

🌎 BioScout, an Australian developer of sensors that alert farmers to fungal pathogens, raised A$6.75m in seed funding. Demea Sustainable Investment and Astanor led, joined by GrainInnovate, GrainCorp Ventures, Hort Innovation Venture Fund, Artesian, and Division Q. axios.link/4q8ixuP

• Osmo, an SF-based storytelling studio, raised $5m in seed funding. Bain Capital Ventures led, joined by Basis Set Ventures, MVP Ventures, Collaborative Fund, and Scott Belsky. axios.link/4wruGMR

• Palette, a Copenhagen, Denmark-based developer of an OS for AI-native teams, raised €3m in pre-seed funding. Ugly Duckling Ventures led, joined by Emblem, Acadian Ventures and a group of angel investors. axios.link/3SqOi5K

• WashWise, an NYC-based clothing care startup, raised $1.2m in pre-seed funding from FJ Labs and Singh Capital. axios.link/3RHj9eb

• Echovane, an SF-based market research platform, raised a $1m pre-seed round led by Titan Capital and Neon Fund. axios.link/4zc3J2j

Private Equity Deals
 

• Amberjack Capital Partners acquired PMV Automation, a Houston-based maker of water management parts, from Flowserve (NYSE: FLS). axios.link/4fXAeIM

• Bernhard Capital Partners agreed to acquire Bowman Consulting Group (Nasdaq: BWMN), a Reston, Va.-based engineering services and program management firm, for around $1b, or $43 per share. axios.link/4goZtoA

• Lindsay Goldberg invested in Alro Steel, a Jackson, Mich.-based distributor of metals and performance plastics. alro.com

• Mari, the PE-backed entertainment firm led by Ari Emanuel, agreed to buy British West End and Broadway theater operator ‌ATG Entertainment for from Providence Equity Partners for a reported $6b. axios.link/3SrgXrm

🔥 New Mountain Capital agreed to acquire Jensen Hughes, a Columbia, Md.-based fire protection engineering and nuclear risk engineering firm, from Gryphon Investors. axios.link/4wW3BT2

• OpenGate Capital agreed to acquire Maersk Training, a provider of safety training and gas safety services, from A.P. Møller - Mærsk. axios.link/3U80j0l

• Second Nature Brands, backed by CapVest Partners, acquired Oregon-based jerky brand Tillamook Country Smoker from Insignia Capital Group. axios.link/4xx8FNA

• Thoma Bravo completed its C$650m acquisition of Kneat (TSX: KSI), an Ireland-based digital validation platform. axios.link/43iy6Wd

• TPG agreed to buy a 61.2% stake in listed South Korean car rental firm Lotte Rental for $925m. axios.link/3SrrSRR

• Velocity FBO Network, backed by Tallvine Partners, acquired SkyPlace FBO, a San Antonio-based fixed base operator services provider for aviation. axios.link/4wMXIr9
 
 
Public Offerings
 

• DayOne, a Singapore-based hyperscale data center operator, filed confidentially for a U.S. IPO that could seek to raise $5b, per Bloomberg. It's raised around $4.5b from firms like SoftBank and Coatue. axios.link/4cxE1LM

• Eaglesky Acquisition, a midmarket SPAC led by Mia Jiang (ex-CFO of Aurelion), filed for a $100m IPO. axios.link/4czkavN

• GigCapital10, an aerospace and TMT SPAC led by Avi Katz, filed for a $220m IPO. axios.link/4bIp9tX

• Gores Holdings XII, a SPAC formed by The Gores Group, filed for a $312m IPO. axios.link/3SmpQT4

• Inflection Point Acquisition VIII, a SPAC led by Michael Blitzer (Kingston Capital Management), filed for a $250m IPO. axios.link/4whmvTa
 
 
Liquidity Events
 

🚑 Jazz Pharmaceuticals (Nasdaq: JAZZ) agreed to acquire Actio Biosciences, a San Diego-based biotech focused on neurological disorders, for $820m upfront (plus up to $500m in earnouts). Actio had raised $121m from Regeneron Ventures, Deerfield, Canaan Partners, Droia Ventures, and Euclidean Capital. axios.link/4xAHOjO

🚑 Skylight Health, a VC-backed multi-specialty care coordination platform, acquired Saffron Health, a YC-backed referral automation company. axios.link/4g2fu2F
 
 
More M&A
 

• Amkor Technology (Nasdaq: AMKR) is considering a stake sale in its China business, per Bloomberg. axios.link/4wRuxmK

• Hanwha of South Korea made a nonbinding bid of up to a $1.2b for Austal USA, a unit of Australian shipbuilder and defense contractor Austal (ASX: ASB). axios.link/4q6yktT

🚑 Teledyne Technologies (NYSE: TDY) agreed to acquire Varex Imaging (Nasdaq: VREX), a Salt Lake City-based X-ray imaging component maker, for $1.1b. axios.link/4g9s3sV

• Webtoon Entertainment (Nasdaq: WBTN) agreed to buy a majority stake in Korean gaming studio RI Games for about $100m. axios.link/4fTdHhC
 
 
Fundraising
 

• First Round Capital is raising $325m for its tenth flagship fund, per an SEC filing. firstround.com

• Exponent raised a €750m single-asset CV for H&MV Engineering, an Irish provider of high-voltage engineering and power infrastructure services. Backers include Apollo S3, Pantheon, and SQ Capital. axios.link/4wkLzc0
 
 
It's Personnel
 

• Marc Brown joined JPMorgan as a managing director, focused on North American venture coverage. He previously led EQT Growth Equity and, before that, spent two decades in corp dev at Microsoft. axios.link/4xCdIwn

• Duran Curis formed Aviara Partners Capital, which will provide equity capital to independent sponsor-led transactions. He previously was founding partner of Ocean Avenue Capital Partners and, before that, was with Drum Capital Management and HRJ Capital. axios.link/4wpWDom
 
 
🏿 Final Numbers
 
Data: Financial Modeling Prep; Chart: Dan Primack/Axios

Nvidia isn't the only chip company in search of more firepower.

  • Intel yesterday upsized a previously announced common stock offering to $20 billion from $15 billion, and priced it at $95 per share.
  • Proceeds are for "general corporate purposes" that may include "capital expenditures and working capital." Intel shares fell over 4% on the news.
